quotes.text: Learn how to save Pix payment details and charge your customers later.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: After the customer authorizes the mandate in their banking app, the SetupIntent moves to a `succeeded` state and the PaymentMethod is attached to the Customer.
If the payment fails after exhausting all of the retries, you can bring your customer back on-session to create a new payment.
Due to scheme restrictions, you can only charge a Pix payment method once per cycle

findings: November 7, 2026 base raw is a two-route selector for Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-14). The exact Checkout and Direct API flows are dated May 6, 2026 (old raw lines 8-12 and 203-207). No November variant bodies were read.
Diff line 871 joins the last old payment-cycle sentence and first November Checkout plus-line. Verified separately at old raw line 870 and new raw line 13.

Root index line 7 routes to Stripe index lines 360, 685 and 748. The Real-Time Payments concept links this source at line 208. The separate Pix concept provides dated related mandate/subscription coverage and already records an optionality distinction at lines 16-18 and 48-50. Preserve these routes and add source-to-concept reciprocal routing.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May save for future recurring use requires a customer-authorized Pix Automático mandate, and the later charge may fail if mandate options are violated (old raw lines 8-10). May Checkout setup initiates without charging; Checkout payment mode adds Pix-specific off-session future use, with payment and banking-app authorization before attachment (old raw lines 72-145).

May Direct API saves without charging using SetupIntent and confirmPixSetup, or pays then saves using PaymentIntent and confirmPixPayment with its own client secret. Verify corresponding Intent status; manually rendering displayed instructions using handleActions false does not activate a mandate or settle payment (old raw lines 248-278, 351-380 and 544-803).

May saved PaymentMethod can fund later attempts subject to mandate conditions, retry and once-per-cycle constraints. Banking app revocation produces mandate.updated and requires a new on-session mandate. Distinguish test authorization/expiry, simulated success/failure, and live Pix-enabled Brazilian bank account for the live flow (old raw lines 147-179 and 805-870).
conflicts: Source line 17 and Real-Time Payments concept line 65 turn both illustrated mandate settings into universal required fields. The May 6 save guide requires the customer-authorized Pix Automático mandate, tells Direct API users to provide mandate options and illustrates amount and payment_schedule on Checkout and Intent paths (old raw lines 8-10, 53-108, 248-278 and 351-380). The May 6 Pix Automático customization table lists defaults of 400 BRL and monthly (raw/stripe-pix-automatico-2025.md lines 53-67). The separate May 13 direct Subscriptions API guide explicitly makes the options optional and shows a sample with amount only (raw/stripe-subscriptions-pix-2026.md lines 688-722, Pix concept lines 16-18 and 48-50). Preserve the save guide's route-specific instructions and examples without asserting either a universal need to pass both fields or universal optionality.

Source lines 22-27 should make the customer authorization and status boundaries discoverable. The May SetupIntent path saves only after customer authorization and verified setup; its return verifies SetupIntent, with no initial payment. The pay-and-save path needs success of payment and bank mandate authorization, checks PaymentIntent on return, and sets off-session future usage at creation (old raw lines 72-145, 351-380, 563-616 and 635-689). `next_action` QR data is an intermediate display artifact, not evidence that either succeeded (old raw lines 691-803).

Source line 37 needs the distinct next-charge conditions, including saved method for the customer, off_session true if the buyer is absent, retry only on failures unrelated to mandate violation, recovery after exhausting retries and the scheme's one-charge-per-specified-cycle limit (old raw lines 147-168, 805-827 and 862-870). A reader attempting a second charge for an add-on in the same cycle must be routed to the stated on-session option.

Preserve the May representation prerequisite Customer vs customer-configured Account, the dated Accounts v2 preview caveat for non-Connect users, and the Direct API example fields name/email/tax ID with stated cross-border legal scope (old raw lines 27-41, 222-236 and 453-485). The test-time success of a mandate is distinct from a future payment success, including test cases where mandates succeed and later payments expire (old raw lines 170-201 and 829-860).

source_assessments.reason: A reader could treat mandatory explicit amount and schedule as universal and attempt repeat off-session add-on charges within a cycle. Correct the May qualification and preserve the separately dated default/optional evidence.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 base capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix/save-payment-details identifies saving Pix details for a later charge and indexes Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-14). It supplies no implementation prerequisites or state transitions. The May 6, 2026 guide explains that a merchant attaches the method to a Customer or customer-configured Account, and the customer authorizes a Pix Automático mandate in their banking app (old raw lines 8-10, 27-41 and 53-55). Checkout setup mode or Direct API SetupIntent saves without an initial charge. Checkout payment mode or a Direct API PaymentIntent using off-session future usage needs successful payment and mandate authorization before saving. On the direct return page, check the matching SetupIntent or PaymentIntent status; QR display and browser return do not prove setup or payment (old raw lines 72-145, 248-278, 351-380 and 563-689). Later qualifying attempts use the saved method and revocation emits mandate.updated (old raw lines 805-827). source-stripe-pix-save-payment-details.md identifies the main options but overstates required mandate customization and omits the cycle limit and successful-authorization boundary.
answers.Q2: The change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix/save-payment-details is presentational/navigation only (new raw lines 9-14) and supplies no substantive rule change. source-stripe-pix-save-payment-details.md should retain the May 6, 2026 instructions and examples for Pix Automático, but avoid a universal requirement that amount and payment_schedule be supplied. The May save guide tells Direct API users to provide mandate options and uses both fields in examples (old raw lines 248-278 and 351-380). The May 6 customization document lists 400 BRL and monthly defaults, and the separate May 13 direct Subscriptions API guide calls the options optional (raw/stripe-pix-automatico-2025.md lines 53-67 and raw/stripe-subscriptions-pix-2026.md lines 688-722). Preserve setup without charge versus payment and save, the cross-border CPF/CNPJ scope, revocation, the once-per-cycle limit and on-session recovery after retries or for an add-on (old raw lines 72-145, 453-485 and 825-870). Preserve root index line 7, Stripe index lines 360, 685 and 748, and Real-Time Payments concept line 208. Add the source backlink and separate November navigation from retained May behavior.
